costNote: Resin, films, aluminum and the energy and freight to convert them into packaging — 81 cents of every sales dollar. Energy and distribution costs spiked late in the quarter, squeezing this line.

footerNote: Amcor is in a fiscal 'transition period' after the Berry Global merger (year-end change); this is the September 2026 quarter, conventionally Q1 FY2027. Sales growth includes significant raw-material cost pass-through (10 points in Flexibles, 4 in Rigid) — charging customers for resin inflation, not volume.

oneTimers.label: Merger costs still flowing
oneTimers.text: Restructuring, transaction and integration costs were $62M in the quarter and amortization of Berry intangibles $140M — the gap between GAAP EPS ($0.52) and adjusted EPS ($0.95) is mostly the merger's tail.

segments.name: Global Flexible Packaging
segments.note: Films and pouches for food, pharma and consumer goods — reported sales +10%, but that was all raw-material pass-through: volumes were flat and organic growth was 0%.

segments.name: Global Rigid Packaging
segments.note: Bottles, containers and closures (the ex-Berry business) — volumes up ~4% excluding non-core/divested lines; organic growth +2%.

takeaways.text: Organic volume growth was just 1% (focus categories +3%) — the 7% sales headline is mostly resin cost pass-through, especially in Flexibles where it added 10 points.
takeaways.title: Growth is thinner than it looks

takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA was flat at $883M despite higher sales: late-quarter energy and distribution inflation ate the gains. Management says mitigation actions keep it out of 2027 results.
takeaways.title: Cost spike ate the growth

takeaways.text: Berry synergy realization is tracking to the three-year $650M target — the core of the investment case while GAAP EPS ($0.52) still carries merger amortization and integration costs.
takeaways.title: Synergies on track

verdict: A merger still being digested: volumes inch up 1%, cost inflation flattens EBITDA, and the synergy clock is the real story.
